approachQuestion.prompt:
Bundle Assembly
There are n positive bundle weights. Joining two bundles costs their sum and replaces them with a bundle of that sum. Return the minimum total cost to end with one bundle. Example: [2,5,9] → 23: joins cost 7 then 16. One bundle [6] costs 0.

1 ≤ n ≤ 200000; weights are positive integers at most 1000000. Input is read-only. All sums and costs fit signed 64 bits. Which approach best meets this contract?
constraints: 1 ≤ n ≤ 200000; weights are positive integers at most 1000000. Input is read-only. All sums and costs fit signed 64 bits.

options.text: Copy weights into a min-heap and build it bottom-up. Repeatedly remove the two smallest weights, add their sum to the total, and insert their sum, until one bundle remains.
options.feedback: The two smallest weights can occupy deepest sibling leaves of an optimal merge tree by exchanging heavier leaves upward. Contracting them leaves the same smaller optimization problem.

options.text: At each join, scan an unsorted working list for its two minima, remove them and append their sum.
options.feedback: This makes the same correct joins but repeatedly scans unaffected bundles.

options.text: Join the two largest available bundles each time.
Sort once, then add each original weight from smallest to largest to one running combined bundle.
options.feedback: For [1,1,1,1], this pays 2+3+4=9; two separate pair joins pay 2+2+4=8.

feedback.reason: The two smallest weights can occupy deepest sibling leaves of an optimal merge tree by exchanging heavier leaves upward. Contracting them leaves the same smaller optimization problem.
details: Copy weights into a min-heap and build it bottom-up. Repeatedly remove the two smallest weights, add their sum to the total, and insert their sum, until one bundle remains.

Joining the two smallest weights avoids charging a large early weight in many later merges. Reinsert their sum as one new bundle. Summing input weights once misses repeated participation in the merge tree.

“Copy weights into a min-heap and build it bottom-up. Repeatedly remove the two smallest weights, add their sum to the total, and insert their sum, until one bundle remains.”: The two smallest weights can occupy deepest sibling leaves of an optimal merge tree by exchanging heavier leaves upward. Contracting them leaves the same smaller optimization problem.
“At each join, scan an unsorted working list for its two minima, remove them and append their sum.”: This makes the same correct joins but repeatedly scans unaffected bundles.
“Join the two largest available bundles each time.”: For [2,5,9], this pays 14+16=30 instead of 23.
“Sort once, then add each original weight from smallest to largest to one running combined bundle.”: For [1,1,1,1], this pays 2+3+4=9; two separate pair joins pay 2+2+4=8.

complexityQuestion.prompt: Analyze A with a copied binary min-heap, bottom-up construction and n−1 joining rounds. Let n be the initial number of bundles. Choose the tightest time and auxiliary-space pair.
constraints: Use the tightest worst-case bound for the whole input unless amortized or expected accounting is explicitly specified. Comparing or moving a record and arithmetic on machine words take constant time.

Exclude supplied input and returned output from auxiliary space. Count working arrays, queues, tables and call stacks. Output storage is separate and is not used as workspace. Heap repairs and traversals are iterative. No hashing is used unless explicitly stated.

options.text: O(n log(n+1)) time, O(n) auxiliary space
O(n log(n+1)) time, O(1) auxiliary space

feedback.reason: Bottom-up heap build precedes n-1 logarithmic merge rounds.
details: Copy/build costs O(n). The n−1 rounds perform root removals and insertions with logarithmic repairs over shrinking heap sizes, totaling O(n log(n+1)) in the worst case. The working heap retains up to n weights. The scalar total is output; n=1 performs no join.
“O(n) time, O(n) auxiliary space”: Construction is linear, but subsequent joins need heap repairs.
“O(n log(n+1)) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: Read-only input requires a working copy.
“O(n²) time, O(n) auxiliary space”: Full scans can be quadratic; roots avoid those scans.
